subject: Information Theory
title: Writing Systems as Encoding
description: A 60-second lesson on Writing Systems as Encoding.

hook.text: English uses 26 letters. Chinese uses thousands of characters. Both encode language—at different levels.

buildup.text: Alphabets encode phonemes—sound units. Character systems encode morphemes—meaning units. Different tradeoffs.

discovery.text: Alphabets need fewer symbols but more per word. Character systems need more symbols but fewer per idea.

twist.text: Information theory predicts the tradeoff: fewer symbols means more bits per symbol but more symbols per message.

climax.text: Both systems converge on similar information density per page. The encoding differs; the throughput matches.

punchline.text: Different encoding, same information. Scripts are design choices.
